items.title_zh: 关于角色混乱的思考
items.summary_en: The other day, I came across " Prompt Injection as Role Confusion " ( via Simon Willison ). It's a really interesting blog-style version of a paper by Charles Ye, Jasmine Cui and Dylan Hadfield-Menell, where they find that LLMs seem to almost ignore 'role' tags like <system> , <user> or <think> , and instead use the tone of text to infer roles. This seems to explain a lot of jailbreaks. The piece is most useful for readers who care about how training choices affect stability, cost, and final model quality in real workflows. For the digest, Thoughts on Role Confusion stands out because it offers enough concrete detail to be useful, while also surfacing the tradeoffs that matter when people evaluate tools, models, and implementation decisions.
items.summary_zh: 前几天，我遇到了“即时注射作为角色混乱”（来自西蒙·威利森）。这是 Charles Ye、Jasmine Cui 和 Dylan Hadfield-Menell 的论文的一个非常有趣的博客风格版本，他们发现 LLMs 似乎几乎忽略了像 <system> 、 <user> 或 <think> 这样的“角色”标签，而是使用文本的语气来推断角色。这似乎可以解释很多越狱的情况。对于关心训练选择如何影响实际工作流程中的稳定性、成本和最终模型质量的读者来说，这篇文章最有用。在摘要中，《关于角色混乱的思考》脱颖而出，因为它提供了足够有用的具体细节，同时还揭示了人们评估工具、模型和实施决策时重要的权衡。

Even Benjamin Franklin's face on a piece of paper can feel like a mere proxy for a database transaction. What makes it notable is the way it connects agent design decisions to practical reliability, tool use, and developer ergonomics. For the digest, cash issuing terminals stands out because it offers enough concrete detail to be useful, while also surfacing the tradeoffs that matter when people evaluate tools, models, and implementation decisions.
